metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_collapse_score: (Mean off-diagonal cosine + 1)/2 for up to 2048 effective ordinary-item embeddings sampled with local seed 42. Approximately 0.5 means mean cosine zero. This measures angular alignment, not recommendation diversity or representation rank. Null for undefined inputs.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-loader-negative score over finite, nonpadding, ordinary-item training positions in at most ten batches. Supplied HSTU features are causal: position t sees sequence[:t+1], not later events.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-order-statistic 10th percentile of sampled pair margins.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of valid sampled pairs with negative score strictly greater than positive score.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of valid sampled pairs with positive-minus-negative score below eps=0.5; depends on score scale.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_category_br: Empty category lists because item categories are unavailable. Position counts remain descriptive; no exposure-adjusted conclusion is supported.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:history_interventions: Frozen-model training-prefix sampled diagnostics, distinct from the host validation benchmark. Up to 32 eligible users/category and two distinct training targets/user, with >=4 context events truncated to model.maxlen. Fallback uses sequence[:t+1] and positive[t], never later events, and reports rows without user confidence intervals. Earlier occurrences of the target remain valid context. One target plus up to 999 unique negatives excludes only prefix-seen items and target, not later events. All variants share candidates. Rank is one plus scores strictly above target plus tied candidates with smaller item ID; target tie frequency counts any equal-scoring other candidate. Greatest absolute nonpadding index supplies readout. Recent/oldest removal delete k=min(3,floor((n-2)/2)) items; final removal deletes one; recent-preserving-final deletes k immediately preceding the final item. Three nonfinal shuffles are averaged within prefix. Rank, reciprocal rank and hit10 effects are perturbed-minus-original: positive rank is worse; positive reciprocal rank/hit10 is better. Recent-minus-oldest compares equal-count deletions; final-minus-prefinal is available only when k=1 for every included prefix. Repeats average within prefixes, prefixes within user (or unidentified row), then users within category. Bootstrap resamples complete category-local users 2000 times with seed 42, retaining all paired outcomes. Intervals condition on fitted weights and fixed candidates. Fallback empirical quantiles describe row effects, not user uncertainty. Candidate counts <=10 make hit10 trivially one. A four-category macro summary is null until all four category user-cluster records are available; do not average category interval endpoints or assume matching local IDs denote the same person. Sensitivity does not identify intent, shortcuts, elapsed-time effects, or generalization; invariance does not establish that history is ignored.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:diagnostic_cost: Wall time includes loader access and all probes. CUDA-event elapsed time measures the diagnostic stream interval, including host-induced idle gaps, not kernel-active GPU time. Peak allocated memory is the absolute PyTorch allocation high-water mark after resetting it at audit entry. History cost_counts record actual sequence evaluations, candidate-score calls and scalar candidate scores. CPU GPU statistics are null. No claim of inexpensive auditing is made.
